hints: Notice the word only - you need a group where every named wave can have its oscillations restricted to one plane.
Recall that polarisation is possible only for transverse waves, where oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of travel.

Sort the waves named here: infrared, visible light, microwaves and radio waves are transverse electromagnetic waves, while sound waves are longitudinal, then check which group has no longitudinal wave.
walkthrough: List what is given: groups made from infrared waves, visible light waves, microwaves, radio waves and sound waves.
State the governing rule: polarisation restricts transverse oscillations to one direction, so only transverse waves can be polarised.

Apply the rule to electromagnetic waves: infrared, visible light, microwaves and radio waves are all transverse electromagnetic waves with oscillating electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to travel, so they can all be polarised.
Apply the rule to sound: sound waves in air are longitudinal with particle oscillations parallel to travel, so they have no transverse plane to restrict and cannot be polarised.
Therefore any group containing sound waves must be rejected, and the group containing three transverse electromagnetic waves with no sound waves is the required group.
